sentences.text: Counsel for Respondent :- Ajai Kumar Singh,G.A.
Heard Sri Arun Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the appellants, learned A.G.A. for the State and learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2.

This criminal appeal has been preferred under Section 14-A (1) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred to as 'SC/ST Act') for setting aside summoning order dated 18.11.2022 passed by Second Additional District and Session Judge/Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Kanpur Dehat in S.S.T. No. 261 of 2019 (Ram Vilas vs. Dev Narayan and others)
under Sections 323, 376/511, 504, 506 IPC read with Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Shivrajpur, District Kanpur Dehat.
It has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellants that the dispute is mainly civil in nature and has been given a criminal colour.

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2 as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the above prayer of the learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and submitted that the opposite party no.
2 moved an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. which was treated as a complaint case and the statements of the complainant, victim and other witnesses were recorded under Sections 200 Cr.P.C. and 202 Cr.P.C.
From the statements of the complainant, victim and other witnesses, prima facie cognizable offence is made out against the appellants.
There is no illegality or irregularity in the impugned order which requires any interference by this Court.
The impugned has been passed in accordance with law.

In view of the above facts and circumstances and having heard learned counsels for the parties and after perusal of record, this Court does not find any illegality in the order impugned, and therefore,
no interference is required by this Court.
Hence, the criminal appeal is dismissed.
